resources.string: Chat with people nearby, with no internet
Works over Bluetooth. No internet or phone number needed.
Tarang needs Bluetooth Low Energy, and this phone does not have it.
Tarang connects phones over Bluetooth, so you can chat with people close by when there is no internet. You do not need a phone number.
Works with other Samvad users and with people using the bitchat app.
People nearby can see your nickname and what you write in the nearby room. Private chats are encrypted.
Messages stay on this phone and are removed when you stop Tarang.
Next, Android will ask to let Samvad find and connect to nearby devices. Samvad does not use your location.
Next, Android will ask for location access, because on Android 11 and older it treats Bluetooth scanning as location. Samvad does not collect or store your location.
While Tarang is on, Bluetooth stays active in the background and uses some battery. Stop Tarang when you do not need it.
Tarang cannot find people without it. You can allow it in the app settings.
Turn on Bluetooth to find people nearby.
Keep Tarang on. People appear here when they are in range.
Everyone nearby can see this. It is not linked to your phone number.
Use letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores.
Say hello. Anyone in range can read what you write here.
Ask a friend to open Tarang or the bitchat app. You need to be within a short distance.
You will stop finding people nearby, and the messages in Tarang will be removed from this phone.
Tarang is off. Turn it on to send messages.
Not sent. Tap to try again.
%s is no longer nearby. You can send messages again when they are back in range.
Only you and %s can read these messages.
Tarang uses Bluetooth to connect phones that are close to each other. Messages can pass through other phones to reach people further away.
Nearby devices can see your nickname and anything you write in the nearby room. Anyone using Tarang or the bitchat app can read it.
Private chats are encrypted between you and one other person. Phones in between can see that a message passed, but not what it says.
Messages stay in this phone\'s memory. They are removed when you stop Tarang or close the app. Samvad servers never see them.
Tarang uses a random ID, not your phone number. Your Samvad name and photo are not shared.
Be careful what you share. People nearby are strangers until you know them.
You will get a new random ID, and people nearby will see you as a new person. Tarang will stop.
Looking for people nearby over Bluetooth.
Shown while Tarang is on, so Bluetooth keeps working.
